summary:
Landing on the lunar south pole is unforgiving. Being just 100 meters off-target can plunge a lander into permanent darkness or block direct-to-Earth communications. Existing mission-planning tools are slow, complex, and locked behind specialist workflows.

Aphelion Lunar Landing Navigator is a zero-install, browser-based web application that cuts site evaluation from hours to seconds. Running entirely client-side with zero server overhead, it combines high-resolution NASA LOLA terrain ray-marching up to 400 kilometers with a dynamic ephemeris engine validated against NASA/JPL Horizons (DE440/DE441) to an exceptional 0.003-degree mean error. To enable rapid site comparisons, Aphelion computes a weighted geometric Balance Score (0–100) across Power (35%), Communications (35%), Night Survival (15%), and Terrain Safety (15%), ensuring fatal flaws cannot be masked.

Aphelion LLN serves both aerospace engineers and classrooms through a unified dual-mode interface. Mission Mode provides a 3D Three.js flight console featuring 360-degree horizon panoramas, real-time lighting simulations, and a seasonal landing calendar, while Learn Mode transforms orbital mechanics into a 10-lesson gamified course powered by live simulations. Grounded in authentic NASA datasets, Aphelion LLN makes aerospace-grade lunar mission planning instantaneous, validated against NASA/JPL Horizons, and universally accessible.
details:
What is Aphelion Lunar Landing Navigator?

Aphelion Lunar Landing Navigator (Aphelion LLN, for short) is a zero-install, browser-based lunar landing navigator designed to help mission planners, researchers, students, and space enthusiasts evaluate landing sites on the Moon,  with a specialized focus on the extreme lighting and communication challenges of the lunar south pole.

What Does it Do and How Does it Work?

At the lunar south pole, the Sun and Earth hover just degrees above the horizon, meaning a single crater rim or ridge can block solar power or cut off direct-to-Earth radio communication for months. Aphelion LLN solves this by turning complex planetary science into an intuitive, three-step workflow: users select one of 36 curated Artemis and CLPS landing sites (or enter custom coordinates and mission dates), run an instant simulation, and receive an overall 0–100 mission suitability score alongside interactive visualizations. Under the hood, a custom ray-marching engine processes raw NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) LOLA elevation grids across 360 directions up to 400 kilometers out to map the exact local terrain horizon. Simultaneously, an in-browser astronomical engine uses Meeus algorithms and IAU 2009 lunar orientation models to compute real-time Sun and Earth positions, cross-referencing them against the terrain horizon to determine exact sunlight percentages, communication windows, and clearance angles.

Benefits & Intended Impact

Traditional lunar illumination and visibility analyses require heavy, specialist-only software that can take hours to configure and run. Aphelion LLN reduces site screening from hours to seconds on any standard laptop or mobile browser. Its intended impact is twofold. First, to accelerate early-stage mission planning and trade-space comparisons for engineers and researchers; and second, to democratize space exploration by giving students and the general public hands-on access to the exact same orbital mechanics and NASA datasets used to plan Artemis missions. The app's Learn mode is available in English and Spanish, and there's a full-app guided tour for first-time users.

Creativity & Design Considerations

What makes Aphelion Lunar Landing Navigator uniquely creative is its dual-mode architecture powered by a single unified physics engine. With one click, users can switch between Mission Mode, a sleek, data-rich flight console featuring live 3D terrain shadows, a 360-degree sky panorama, year-long season calendars, and CSV data exports; and Learn Mode, an interactive educational hub featuring 10 guided lessons, hands-on labs, quizzes, and rank progression powered by live simulations. When designing the platform, our team carefully balanced scientific rigor with accessibility. We prioritized client-side performance so the app requires zero backend servers or installations, ensured transparent data provenance by citing every formula and dataset directly in the interface, and enforced strict automated validation against NASA/JPL Horizons ephemerides, achieving a mean angular accuracy of 0.003 degrees.

Tools, Languages, & Software Used

  • Frontend & 3D Visualization: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (ES6+), and three.js (r170) for rendering the interactive 3D Moon globe, Earth orientation, and local terrain relief.
  • Core Engine & Algorithms: Custom client-side JavaScript implementing Meeus astronomical algorithms, IAU 2009 lunar coordinate models, and a 360-degree terrain horizon ray-marcher.
  • Data Processing & DevOps: Node.js and Python scripts to process raw NASA LRO LOLA elevation grids, hosted statically on GitHub Pages with automated GitHub Actions verification checks against JPL Horizons reference tables.
  • NASA & Partner Data: NASA LRO LOLA digital elevation models (PDS Geosciences Node), NASA/JPL Horizons (DE440/DE441), NASA SVS Moon 3D models, NASA Earth Observatory Blue Marble imagery, NASA Moon Trek, and ASU LROC QuickMap.
  • Super Intelligence (SI) tools: SI tools were used in order to accelerate the development of our project, in areas like code and data. Check our README for precise details on how SI tools were used: https://github.com/starvulkan/Aphelion-Lunar-Landing-Navigator#use-of-super-intelligence-tools

Try Aphelion LLN!
